subject: Urgent: ZeroCare production 5xx/429 spike — immediate mitigation
messages:
From: Sarah Lim <sarah@zerocare.com>
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@zerocare.com
Date: 2028-07-21T08:15:22-07:00
Subject: Production errors — sudden 5xx/429 spike impacting API calls

Nikhil,

We started seeing a big spike in 5xx/429 responses from the Redwood endpoint for our dedicated pool about 07:50 PDT. Error rate climbed to ~12% for ~10 minutes and several client timeouts have cascaded into retry storms on our side. This is affecting our clinical ingestion pipeline and patient-facing chat.

Key details:
- Environment: ZeroCare prod (dedicated pool: zc-prod-pool-3)
- Symptoms: 5xx (internal server errors) + 429 rate increase; many requests hit timeouts ~10–12s
- Our retry logic began amplifying traffic when responses started failing

We attached a sample of our client logs and a short curl trace. Can you confirm whether this is an autoscale lag or something else with the Dedicated pool? This is high priority for our ops and leadership. Please escalate.

Attachments: [attachment: client-curl-trace.txt (text/plain)]

—
Sarah Lim
Head of Platform Ops, ZeroCare Health
sarah@zerocare.com
+1 415-555-0189

From: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Lim <sarah@zerocare.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-21T08:28:05-07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors — sudden 5xx/429 spike impacting API calls

Sarah — thanks for the heads up and the logs. I’m opening an incident now and looping in ops and engineering. Immediate plan:

1) On-call will check pool health and autoscale status (ETA 10m)
2) We’ll temporarily increase min replicas and enable fast-scale policy for the pool
3) If necessary, we’ll fail over some traffic to a quantized fallback model to reduce GPU memory pressure

Can you confirm whether any client-side deploys coincided with 07:45–08:00? Also, please keep your retry window widened (linear backoff) while we remediate — aggressive retries will worsen the overload.

I’ll update in thread as we have findings. Apologies for the disruption — we’ll prioritize.

—
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
(650) 555-0123

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-21T08:42:33-07:00
Subject: Fwd: ZeroCare production 5xx/429 spike — initial ops notes

Internal — quick findings from the first 15m of triage:
- Metrics: pool zc-prod-pool-3 shows a steep queue depth spike at 07:46; autoscaler did not provision additional nodes until ~07:58 (12m lag)
- Observed node drain events around 07:44–07:47; nodes reported driver restarts that caused ephemeral loss of GPU capacity
- Pool cushion (reserved slack) was effectively 0 due to sustained high utilization pre-incident

Proposed immediate actions (doing now):
- Increase pool min_replicas by +2 and bump cushion to 20% (temp)
- Switch autoscaler mode to "fast_scale" for this pool to reduce cold-provision lag
- Push temporary routing rule to divert 30% of low-priority traffic to the quantized-ggml fallback model to reduce per-token GPU memory pressure

Attachments: [attachment: autoscales-log-snippet.txt (text/plain)]

I’ll post when the scale changes are in. If we still see 5xx after cushion + fast_scale, we should consider rolling back the kernel update that hit zc-prod-nodes at 07:35 (recent infra change).

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-21T09:05:10-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: ZeroCare production 5xx/429 spike — initial ops notes

Confirming root cause from kernel traces and driver logs: several nodes experienced a GPU driver restart sequence after a recent OS package pulled an updated driver. That triggered ephemeral evictions and reduced the available GPU count, which combined with a low cushion and normal traffic patterns resulted in queueing and 5xx/429 bursts as the autoscaler lagged.

Actions taken (09:00):
- Rolled back the driver update on the affected node group
- Increased min_replicas by 3 for zc-prod-pool-3 and enabled fast_scale policy
- Applied retry-throttling at the edge for ZeroCare tenant to cap client-side retry amplification (drop-to-200ms later-retry window)

I’ve uploaded the detailed traces to the incident bundle.

Attachments: [attachment: debug-trace-20280721.zip (application/zip)]

If we see repeated restarts after rollback, we’ll schedule a coordinated node reboot window.

From: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Lim <sarah@zerocare.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-21T09:17:45-07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors — sudden 5xx/429 spike impacting API calls

Sarah — short update and customer-facing remediation summary:

What happened (brief):
- A recent driver update caused ephemeral GPU node restarts which depleted the Dedicated pool capacity. Autoscaler lag + zero cushion allowed queue depth to spike, producing increased 5xx and 429 responses. Client retries amplified the effect.

Immediate mitigations (completed):
- Rolled back driver update on affected node group
- Increased pool min_replicas and enabled fast_scale for zc-prod-pool-3
- Enabled temporary routing to quantized fallback for lower-cost requests (30% divert)
- Applied edge retry throttling for your tenant to reduce amplification

Next steps (we own these):
- Full postmortem and timeline (JIRA: INF-4729) — delivering within 48 hours
- Root-cause RCA and permanent autoscaler tuning to avoid >5m provisioning lag
- Credit proposal for downtime impact — I’ll share terms by EOD

We’re continuing to monitor. Can you confirm whether your error rate has returned to baseline from your side? If it’s still elevated, we’ll keep the fast_scale policy on and expand cushion further.

Incident refs: HubSpot 0045321, JIRA INF-4729

—
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Lim <sarah@zerocare.com>
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@zerocare.com
Date: 2028-07-21T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors — sudden 5xx/429 spike impacting API calls

Nikhil — thanks for the quick handling and the clear notes. Ops reports error rate back to baseline as of ~09:10 and our ingestion jobs have recovered. Appreciate the temporary routing and throttling — that stopped the retry amplification on our end.

Please include a clear SLA-impact statement and credit calculation in the postmortem. Our security team will want the list of node images and driver versions that were rolled back for their records.

—
Sarah
Head of Platform Ops, ZeroCare Health
